_readme: The validator's geometric thresholds, split by the one thing that changes what
can be done with them: whether there is a measurement behind them.
`normative` come from a norm or a published experiment — WCAG 2.2, the expert
percentiles from Table 2 of Mooney et al. (GD 2025), the C4 checklist. Changing
one of these isn't configuring, it's disagreeing with the source; so the source
is written alongside, and whoever changes it has to swap the citation too.
`calibratable` are the ones the rubric (#8) flagged in place as an 'engineering
default': plausible numbers nobody measured. #18 decides these become
config — not because configuring is good, but because an unmeasured number
hard-coded inside an `if` is indistinguishable from a measured one, and the
difference is exactly what the rubric bothered to record. Once it becomes a
named key, the number carries `because: null` — the empty field is the request
for measurement, visible to whoever calibrates it.

nodeResolutionQ1.source: Mooney et al., GD 2025, eq. (9) + Table 2 (expert Q1)

crossingsQ1.source: Mooney et al., GD 2025, eq. (3) + Table 2

crossingAngleQ1.source: Mooney et al., GD 2025, eq. (2) + Table 2

idealCrossingAngle.source: Huang, Eades, Hong & Lin (JVLC 2014); adopted by Dunne et al. 2015 and greadability.js

minCrossingAngle.source: Mooney et al., GD 2025 — below this the crossing stops being legible

minIncidentAngle.source: rubric A6.1 — below this two incident edges are indistinguishable to the eye

angularResolutionQ1.source: Mooney et al., GD 2025, eq. (1) + Table 2

nodeUniformityQ1.source: Mooney et al., GD 2025, eq. (10) + Table 2

edgeLengthUniformityQ1.source: Mooney et al., GD 2025, eq. (4) + Table 2

orthogonalityQ1.source: Mooney et al., GD 2025, Table 2 — below this it's a disordered mix of angles

graphicComplexityTarget.source: Moody, Physics of Notations — span of absolute judgement ≈ 6 categories

graphicComplexityFail.source: Moody, Physics of Notations — 7-8 is warn, above is fail

elementsTarget.source: Ghoniem/Fekete/Castagliola; Yoghourdjian et al. (arXiv:1809.00270) — cutoff at 20

maxDensity.source: Yoghourdjian et al. — 78% of studies use density <10%

minEdgeLabelFontSize.rubric: A3.9 — 'practical floor below which text stops being legible in print/slide'; the rubric warns this is NOT a WCAG rule (WCAG governs contrast, not size)

maxProximity.rubric: A4.7 — 'Threshold value is an engineering default, not measured'

bendsTarget.rubric: A5.3 — 'The value 2 is an engineering default'; 1 is the declared target

bendsWarn.rubric: A5.3 — the number the rubric flagged

bendAngleTarget.rubric: A5.4 — derived from Gestalt/continuity, with no experiment of its own

minConsistentFlow.rubric: A5.7 — 'The value 0.90 is an engineering default'

minAlignment.rubric: A6.4 — 'The value 70% is an engineering default'

gridStep.rubric: A6.4 — the grid step is an example in the rubric ('e.g.: 8 px')

minDeltaE00.rubric: A7.4 — 'engineering operationalization (the W3C does not prescribe ΔE). Mark as a calibratable default'

gapBetweenBoxes.rubric: A3.1 — 'gap ≥ 8 px (or ≥ 0.25 × icon height)'; the rubric gives two forms of the same number and does not pick one

groupPadding.because: CALIBRATED AT THE #23 RECERTIFICATION, and the 12 was a mirror. #18 inherited the number from the `PAD = 12` that #11's engine used, and under that regime the check measured the engine against itself. With the theme layer (#13) the engine started deriving the gap from a base-8 grid — and the measurement leaves no room for interpretation: with threshold 12, A4.1 flags 77 occurrences across 14 of the 15 models in the corpus, and ALL of them report exactly 8 px; with threshold 8, it flags zero. None of them is defective containment, all of them are the new scale. And 8 isn't a number picked to make the test pass: `gridStep` and `gapBetweenBoxes` already held 8 in this same table, and the theme's base 8 comes from the AWS normative icons (48 and 40 px, A9/A6 of #5) and the N7 floor of 0.05" ≈ 4.8 px, whose next step is 8. The three numbers now agree instead of one contradicting the other two. What A4.1 protects — child INSIDE parent, without touching — stays protected; A4.2, untouched, is what guards membership.
groupPadding.rubric: A4.1 — minimum inner padding on all four sides

labelPadding.rubric: A3.2 — 'padding of 2 px' on the intersection of text bounding boxes

aspectRatioTolerance.rubric: A6.3 — 'differs from the canvas ratio by more than 20%'

maxFanOut.rubric: A8.3 — the rubric's U8 lists deg ≤ 8 among the "engineering defaults"; the derivation from A6.1 is reasoning, not measurement

inkCoverage.rubric: A8.4 — the rubric's U8 lists the coverage range among the "engineering defaults"; the rubric itself calls it a diagnostic signal, not a failure

avgCharWidth.rubric: none — it's the validator's own. Average glyph advance in Helvetica 12px (~0.55em). The engine calibrated 6.7 independently (resolve.cjs); the agreement is expected, and the check's value isn't in the constant but in composing label boxes and intersecting them, which the engine never does

lineHeight.rubric: none — it's the validator's own. Line height for a leaf label at 12px

minLabelHeight.rubric: none — it's the validator's own. Floor for a single-line label band

maxLabelWidth.rubric: none — it's the validator's own. Width at which the service icon's label wraps

titleBandHeight.rubric: none — it's the validator's own. Title band reserved at the top of a container
